title: Find the path, not just its length
description:
Write `findPath(map, sx, sy, tx, ty)`. It returns the tiles of a shortest path from `(sx, sy)` to `(tx, ty)`, **including both ends**, as `(x, y)` pairs in order from start to target. Moves are up, down, left and right; `'#'` tiles are walls; every other character is walkable.

If the target cannot be reached, return an empty vector. If the start is the target, return just that one tile.

When several shortest paths exist, any of them is accepted: the tests check that your path is valid and as short as possible.

Use a breadth-first search, recording for each tile the tile it was reached from.
hints: Keep one number per tile saying where it was reached from: its index `y * w + x`, `-1` for the start, and something else (such as `-2`) for "not reached yet". The same array then doubles as the visited marker.
When the target comes out of the queue, follow `cameFrom` back from it until you reach `-1`, pushing each tile; then reverse the vector.
To turn an index back into a tile: `x = index % w`, `y = index / w`.
